findings.description: The gate requires every argument to have help, but the docstring says the section is written if at least one argument is documented. A command with one documented and one undocumented argument now loses its whole Positional arguments section.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a command with two Arguments, one with help='...' and one with no help. The old code listed the documented one. The new all(...) check is False, so nothing is written. The user sees no positional argument documentation at all, a regression from the previous behavior and a contradiction of the new docstring.

findings.description: all() over an empty list is True, so a command with no arguments now renders an empty 'Positional arguments' heading.
findings.rationale: Trigger: any command with no Argument parameters, where format_arguments is called during help generation. args is empty, so all(...) returns True and the section is opened with zero records. The user sees a spurious heading in every such command's --help output.

findings.description: The fallback '(arg.make_metavar(ctx), "")' runs even for arguments whose get_help_record returned None because they are hidden, so hidden arguments now appear in help output.
findings.rationale: Trigger: an Argument with hidden=True and help set. get_help_record returns None for hidden params, and the fallback then adds its metavar as a visible row. The user sees an argument the author chose to hide, which changes help output for hidden parameters.
